real_objective: Reduce the literal Opus 5.5 capability target to causally intrinsic model behavior without losing any real behavior and without requiring premature completeness of the model interface alphabet.
material_premises: Current first-party tool documentation says the model emits requests while client code or Anthropic servers execute tool operations.
For user-defined client tools the model sees schema and returned result, not implementation code.
Current Opus 5.5 documentation exposes thinking blocks/signatures as load-bearing carried-forward state in tool-use loops.
Current canonical intrinsic-profile projection already separates Opus55-served behavior from fallback/classifier/tool-backend behavior.
A causal quotient over executor variants can be stated relative to the true model-visible state I_STAR, so it remains sound when I_STAR gains newly discovered channels.

conclusion.core: Intrinsic Opus tool capability is invariant under substitutions of external executors that preserve the model-visible trace relative to the true load-bearing model state I_STAR.
conclusion.repair_over_v1: Do not freeze I_STAR to text plus tool blocks. Thinking/signature and any later verified load-bearing channel join I_STAR without changing the quotient argument.
conclusion.deletion: External backend implementation variants do not generate distinct intrinsic Opus capability obligations merely because Opus can control them.
conclusion.preserve: All model-side orchestration, semantic judgment, state handling, direct modalities, and profile-specific Opus55-served behaviors remain target obligations.
conclusion.terminal_truth: This is target-space compression, not terminal completion; literal target completeness and current acceptance residuals remain open.

rejected_material_alternatives.reason: Falsified as a completeness assumption by the signed thinking-state channel counterexample.
Causal misattribution and artificial open-ended target growth.
Unsound; Opus55-generated refusals, scope judgment, profile-specific served behavior, and other intrinsic behavior must remain.
No complete target-domain witness follows from this theorem.

uncertainties: I_STAR is not yet proven completely enumerated.
Private or undocumented first-party surfaces may reveal additional load-bearing channels.
Lossless mapping from the intrinsic behavior universe to current family/evaluation structure remains separate.
Literal finality still requires a sound complete target-domain premise.
assumptions: First-party documentation correctly describes the checked public execution boundaries.
Capability attribution is causal with respect to model-visible and carried-forward state.
Trace equivalence is evaluated over all load-bearing model-visible state, not merely displayed text.
non_goals: No claim thinking signature bytes themselves are a capability to clone.
No acceptance, family, capability, or ownership promotion.
supersession_conditions: A verified Opus55 behavior causally depends on executor internals without any model-visible or carried-forward trace difference.
The terminal target is explicitly changed from Opus55 capability to complete deployed-system cloning.
A stronger verified causal target theorem subsumes this quotient.
